context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop serialising the raw `memories` records. Map each memory to an explicit allow-list of the fields the client needs before sending it, for example `const toMemoryDto = (m) => ({ id: m.id, title: m.title, content: m.content, createdAt: m.createdAt })`, then respond with `res.status(200).json({ status: 'success', data: memories.map(toMemoryDto) })`. Exclude internal or sensitive fields such as `userId`, owner or tenant identifiers, embeddings, internal flags, audit fields, and any nested relations, unless the requester is entitled to them. Where entitlement varies by role or ownership, apply the field filter conditionally in the same helper so the rule lives in one place. Apply the same DTO mapper in every route or controller that returns memory records (list, get-by-id, search, create/update responses, and any export or websocket broadcast) so that access-control limits are consistent across endpoints. Add a test for each route that asserts the response contains only the allowed keys and omits the restricted ones.
